title: Supported perfect approximation extends across an affine open
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with an open covering $Y=U\cup V$. Assume that $U$ is quasi-compact, $V$ is affine, and $U\cap V$ is quasi-compact. If $\mathsf A(U)$ holds, then $\mathsf A(Y)$ holds, where $U$ and $V$ carry their open subscheme structures and $\mathsf A$ is the uniform supported perfect approximation property [def-sfb-supported-perfect-approximation-property].

proof.text: Fix a closed $T\subseteq Y$ with retrocompact complement. The complement of $T\cap U$ in $U$ is retrocompact: every affine open of $U$ is also an affine open of $Y$. Choose a witness $r_U$ for $\mathsf A(U)$ at $T\cap U$, and enlarge it to be nonnegative. Enlarging a witness preserves its property: $a$-pseudo-coherence implies $b$-pseudo-coherence for $b\ge a$ by the same local approximation, and the support condition becomes stronger when its lower endpoint decreases. Put $T'=T\setminus U$, closed in $Y$ and contained in $V$. The correct complement formula is $V\setminus T'=(V\setminus T)\cup(U\cap V)$. Both opens on the right are quasi-compact, the first by retrocompactness and the second by hypothesis; their union is quasi-compact. Choose a finite affine cover of this complement with $s\ge0$ members. Set $r=r_U+s$, a number depending only on $Y,T$ and the fixed cover.

source.place: Tag 08ER, lemma-induction-step, proof (with the bound and endpoints corrected as reported).

proof.text: Fix $m$ and an admissible $E$: it is $(m-r)$-pseudo-coherent, lies in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, and is supported on $T$ in degrees $\ge m-r$. On each open in its pseudo-coherence cover, cohomology vanishes above the maximum of $m-r$ and the upper bound of the strictly perfect approximation. Quasi-compactness of $U$ gives a finite subcover of $U$ and hence an integer $h$ with $H^i(E)|_U=0$ for $i>h$. Prove the approximation conclusion, simultaneously for all such $E$, by induction on $\max(0,h-(m-s)+1)$. This uses an upper bound, not a largest nonzero degree, so also covers $E|_U=0$. Exact restriction commutes with cohomology and preserves the local defining approximations.

source.place: Tag 08ER, lemma-induction-step, proof (with the bound and endpoints corrected as reported).

proof.text: In the base case $h<m-s$, $H^i(E)|_U=0$ for $i\ge m-s$. Since $r\ge s$, the support condition outside $T$ also holds in these degrees. Thus $H^i(E)$ is supported on $T'$ for $i\ge m-s$. The restriction $E|_V$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent by monotonicity, because $r\ge0$. Apply the affine approximation theorem to $V,T',m,s$: its required support range $i\ge m-s+1$ follows from the stronger bound just obtained. This gives a perfect $B$ supported on $T'$ and $b:B\to E|_V$ inducing isomorphisms above $m$ and a surjection at $m$.

source.place: Tag 08ER, lemma-induction-step, proof (with the bound and endpoints corrected as reported).

proof.text: Let $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$. The supported-open pushforward theorem says that $Rj_*B$ is perfect and $j_!B\cong Rj_*B$. Let $P=j_!B$ and let $v:P\to E$ correspond to $b$ under the derived extension-by-zero adjunction. Exactness of extension by zero gives $H^i(P)=j_!H^i(B)$. Its stalks are those of $H^i(B)$ on $V$ and zero outside $V$, so $P$ is supported on $T'\subseteq T$. On $V$, the map $v$ is $b$ under the adjunction unit; this unit is an isomorphism, as follows from the inside-stalk unit formula (the restriction back to $V$ is the identity). Outside $V$, both $H^i(P)$ and $H^i(E)$ vanish for $i\ge m$, because $T'\subset V$ and $m\ge m-s$. Consequently $v$ has the required cohomology isomorphisms and surjection everywhere. The stalk criterion detects the isomorphisms; exact stalks identify the cokernel of the degree-$m$ map as zero, hence that map is surjective.

source.place: Tag 08ER, lemma-induction-step, proof (with the bound and endpoints corrected as reported).

proof.text: Suppose $h\ge m-s$. Then $h-r_U\ge m-r$, so $E|_U$ is $(h-r_U)$-pseudo-coherent and supported on $T\cap U$ in degrees $\ge h-r_U$. Apply $\mathsf A(U)$ at approximation degree $h$, obtaining $p:A\to E|_U$ with $A$ perfect supported on $T\cap U$, an isomorphism in degrees $>h$, and a surjection in degree $h$. In particular $H^i(A)=0$ for $i>h$. Put $W=U\cap V$. The affine supported extension theorem on $V$, with closed support $T\cap V$, supplies a perfect supported $Q$ and an isomorphism $c:Q|_W\cong(A\oplus A[1])|_W$. Its hypotheses hold because $W$ is quasi-compact and $V\setminus T$ is quasi-compact. Apply the affine perfect-map lifting theorem to the composite $Q|_W\xrightarrow{c}(A\oplus A[1])|_W\xrightarrow{\mathrm{pr}_1}A|_W\xrightarrow{p}E|_W$. Replace $Q$ by the supplied perfect $Q_1$, still supported on $T\cap V$, and replace $c$ by $c\circ\beta|_W$. The resulting map $b:Q_1\to E|_V$ satisfies $b|_W=p|_W\circ\mathrm{pr}_1\circ c$.

source.place: Tag 08ER, lemma-induction-step, proof (with the bound and endpoints corrected as reported).

proof.text: Glue $A\oplus A[1]$ on $U$ and $Q_1$ on $V$ using $c^{-1}$ and the compatible maps $p\circ\mathrm{pr}_1,b$. The derived open gluing theorem gives $a:R\to E$ whose restriction to $U$ is $p\circ\mathrm{pr}_1$ and whose restriction to $V$ is $b$. Finite sums and shifts preserve perfectness, so the two restrictions are perfect. Their strictly perfect local covers together cover $Y$, proving $R$ perfect by definition. Their vanishing stalks prove support on $T$. On $U$, $H^i(R)=H^i(A)\oplus H^{i+1}(A)$, which vanishes for $i>h$, and $H^h(a)$ is surjective. Perfect objects are pseudo-coherent by the perfect-to-pseudo-coherent theorem, and pseudo-coherent scheme objects have quasi-coherent cohomology. In particular $R\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$.

source.place: Tag 08ER, lemma-induction-step, proof (with the bound and endpoints corrected as reported).

proof.text: Complete $a$ to a distinguished triangle $R\to E\to E_1\to R[1]$. A perfect object is locally strictly perfect, so its local identity approximation makes $R$ $(m-r+1)$-pseudo-coherent. Apply part (1) of the ringed-site pseudo-coherence triangle theorem on the small Zariski ringed site, whose local strictly perfect definition is exactly the scheme definition: $E_1$ is $(m-r)$-pseudo-coherent. The quasi-coherent derived property is closed under shifts and triangle middle terms; apply it with support equal to $Y$ to the rotated triangle $E\to E_1\to R[1]$. Hence $E_1\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$. The cohomology long exact sequence on $U$ gives $H^i(E_1)|_U=0$ for $i\ge h$, using the surjection at $h$ and the vanishing above $h$ of $R|_U,E|_U$. At a stalk outside $T$, all cohomology stalks of $R$ vanish, so the same sequence identifies $H^i(E_1)_y$ with $H^i(E)_y$. Thus $E_1$ satisfies the same support bound. The induction hypothesis at upper bound $h-1$ now gives an approximation $v_1:P_1\to E_1$ at degree $m$, with $P_1$ perfect supported on $T$.

source.place: Tag 08ER, lemma-induction-step, proof (with the bound and endpoints corrected as reported).

proof.text: Let $d:E_1\to R[1]$ be the connecting morphism. Complete $d\circ v_1$ and rotate to obtain a distinguished triangle $R\to P\to P_1\xrightarrow{d\circ v_1}R[1]$. Apply TR3 to the rotated triangles starting with $P_1\to R[1]$ and $E_1\to R[1]$, using $v_1$ and the identity of $R[1]$, and shift the third map back. This yields $v:P\to E$ and a morphism from the upper triangle to $R\to E\to E_1\to R[1]$ whose outer components are $1_R,v_1$. Two-out-of-three gives that $P$ is perfect. At a point outside $T$, the upper triangle's exact cohomology sequence has zero outer stalks in every degree, proving all stalks of $H^i(P)$ there are zero.

source.place: Tag 08ER, lemma-induction-step, proof (with the bound and endpoints corrected as reported).

proof.text: Check the comparison on stalks at any fixed point, using the long exact sequences of this triangle morphism. For $i\ge m$, map $z\in H^i(E)$ to $z_1\in H^i(E_1)$ and lift $z_1$ to $x_1\in H^i(P_1)$ through $H^i(v_1)$. Its boundary in $H^{i+1}(R)$ is zero by commutativity, so lift $x_1$ to $x\in H^i(P)$. The difference $z-H^i(v)x$ comes from $H^i(R)$; adjust $x$ by that class. This proves surjectivity. If $i>m$ and $H^i(v)x=0$, injectivity of $H^i(v_1)$ says $x$ comes from $a\in H^i(R)$. Since $a$ maps to zero in $H^i(E)$, it is the boundary of some $b\in H^{i-1}(E_1)$. Surjectivity of $H^{i-1}(v_1)$, valid since $i-1\ge m$, lifts $b$ to $H^{i-1}(P_1)$. The upper exact sequence makes the image of $a$ in $H^i(P)$ zero, so $x=0$. Thus the stalk maps are bijective above $m$ and surjective at $m$. Stalk detection gives the sheaf isomorphisms; exact stalks show the degree-$m$ cokernel has all stalks zero, hence is zero. This proves that $v$ is an approximation and completes the induction. Since the fixed $r=r_U+s$ works for every $m,E$, $\mathsf A(Y)$ holds.
